analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md (the pair's coordinated auto-update section, lines ~534-583, and the 'Not yet in this build' list at 644-646) and docs/reference/configuration.md line 410 (DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK now also read by ClusterServiceCommand.supervisorConfiguration and skipping the cluster pair's update). No code or controls changed in the supplied evidence, so I found no concrete security regression.

The docs describe a new behavior whose implementation is outside the supplied units: each Mac's cluster service polls the coordinator for the latest release every 30 minutes, then downloads, verifies and stages it. After a drain of up to 120 seconds, both Macs install and restart. The documented rollback is three failed starts within 10 minutes, plus a pre-restart start check that restores the previous release and quarantines the new one. This touches T-043 (the watchdog/rollback authority is the same replaceable binary), T-013 and T-034 (binary integrity, release registry A-011), and TB-002 (the coordinator is the trusted release source). The docs say 'downloads, verifies and stages' but do not state what verification occurs (signature, hash against the coordinator-registered release, code identity). The code must be checked to confirm the pair's updater reuses the single-Mac updater's verification and does not accept an unverified or downgraded release.

A second unverified contract is that the 'cluster approval' re-registration after an update needs correct App Attest/qualification generation handling (T-053, T-054). The quarantine and rollback state files are also an integration question, since they are same-UID-writable and covered by T-043. The documented update slot is derived from the cluster ID and the 'never cancels a request' drain is availability-oriented (T-010, T-057). No changed line weakens a stated control, so there are no findings, but the implementing Swift code (ClusterServiceCommand, cluster updater) was not supplied and deserves review for updater verification, downgrade protection and the DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK opt-out being honoured.
